findings.desc: DONE-required timeout classification is not implemented across the promised layers. `runDoneRequiredValidation` records a command timeout as a FAIL receipt, but `handlers/done-required-validation.ts` maps every non-PASS to result=failed and always emits timeoutLayer=null; `done_prepare` then parses that as failed and omits timeoutLayer. The CLI idle/max watchdog in `cli-engine.ts` still calls process.exit(2), so direct/done_prepare JSON receives no terminal result at all for idle/max expiry. Even successful done_prepare reused/executed output omits timeoutLayer=null because `donePrepareJsonResult` only adds a recognized non-null token. This contradicts CHK-001/003 requirements for result=timed_out and timeoutLayer=command|phase|idle|max, and leaves the JSON contract unable to distinguish timeout from validation failure.
findings.resolvedReason: Repro: real subprocess matrices force command, phase, CLI idle, and CLI max expiry and inspect JSON plus shell status. Root cause: command receipts collapsed timeout into generic failure, done_prepare omitted routine watchdog attribution, and cli-engine force-exited before handlers could settle. Fix: timeout receipts now map to result=timed_out/timeoutLayer=command; AbortController-backed structured watchdogs propagate idle|max to direct validation and done_prepare; phase remains phase-attributed; structured failed/timed_out/blocked output stays parseable and exits nonzero. ReproTest: npm --prefix packages/main run build; node packages/main/dist/tasks/validate-progress-heartbeat-smoke.js; node packages/main/dist/tasks/done-prepare-closure-heartbeat-smoke.js. Both smoke commands PASS at HEAD a6cefb0 and assert nonzero timeout status plus immediate rerun cleanup.

findings.desc: The trusted metadata-only reuse lineage checks only the net tree diff (`git diff --name-only evidenceHead..currentHead`), not paths touched by every intervening commit. A descendant history can modify a code/config path and later restore it; that path disappears from the net diff, so this function can classify the lineage as trusted-story-metadata-descendant. This violates the documented and CHK-002 requirement that every intervening changed path be trusted metadata and that any intervening code/config path refuse reuse. Enumerate changed paths per commit across the ancestry range (including deletes/renames) or explicitly narrow the contract to final-tree equivalence.
findings.resolvedReason: Repro: create evidence at an ancestor, modify a non-metadata path in one intervening commit, restore it in a later commit, then evaluate reuse; the former net diff hid the touched path. Root cause: lineage trust used only git diff evidenceHead..currentHead instead of enumerating paths touched by every commit. Fix: reuse now verifies ancestry, enumerates rev-list commits, reads each commit with diff-tree --no-renames, rejects any untrusted touched path including modify-then-revert and rename history, and rechecks HEAD to close TOCTOU. ReproTest: node packages/main/dist/tasks/done-required-validation-smoke.js; node scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs. Both PASS at HEAD a6cefb0 and mechanically cover per-commit lineage, non-ancestor, code/config paths, modify-revert, rename, and concurrent HEAD movement.

Reuse tests call the evaluator only and never exercise done_prepare default reuse, reuseFreshDoneRequired=false, fresh/stale/missing validate=false immutability, structured failure/timeout/block outputs, malformed/unreadable evidence, full lineage matrix, or TOCTOU. Direct-handler tests run an instant child and synchronous throwing sink only: no silent heartbeat past idle, real direct CLI watchdog, explicit idle/max, passing and failing rejected sinks, boundary ordering, descendant cleanup, lock reacquisition, or late-heartbeat race. Add table-driven budget tests and hermetic real-CLI fixtures per omitted intent, then bind each evidence ref to assertions that actually exist.

findings.desc: Malformed or unreadable existing done-required evidence aborts the recovery path instead of being classified stale and replaced. evaluateDoneRequiredPreRunReuse calls evaluateDoneRequiredEvidence without a containment boundary (done-prepare-validation-reuse.ts:97), while StoryStore deliberately rethrows JSON parse/read errors for this artifact (store.ts:236-241). Both direct done_required_validate (done-required-validation.ts:46) and done_prepare validate=false/validate=true invoke that evaluator before they can execute or report structured status. A truncated JSON file therefore throws out of the command; even a valid JSON object with missing arrays can trigger TypeErrors in the canonical evaluator. This violates the fail-closed-but-convergent contract: malformed evidence must yield existingEvidenceBasis=stale with a refusal reason, validate=false must remain observation-only, and validate=true/direct validation must be able to run once and overwrite bad evidence. Catch artifact/evaluator shape/read failures in the pre-run reuse wrapper, return reusable=false/stale with a stable malformed-or-unreadable reason, and ensure execution does not depend on parsing prior evidence.
findings.resolvedReason: Repro: replace done-required-evidence.json with truncated JSON and then with a valid object missing required arrays; invoke validate=false observation and validate=true/direct execution. Root cause: evaluateDoneRequiredPreRunReuse allowed store read/parse and canonical evaluator shape exceptions to escape before execution. Fix: the reuse wrapper contains unreadable/malformed artifact and evaluator failures, returns reusable=false with existingEvidenceBasis=stale and stable evidence-malformed-or-unreadable refusal, while validate=false remains non-mutating and validate=true/direct validation overwrite bad evidence with a fresh receipt. ReproTest: node packages/main/dist/tasks/done-required-validation-smoke.js; node packages/main/dist/tasks/done-prepare-closure-heartbeat-smoke.js. Both PASS at HEAD a6cefb0 and assert malformed JSON/shape classification, byte-for-byte validate=false immutability, and successful recovery execution.

findings.desc: F-001 remains incomplete for done_prepare CLI idle/max timeouts. cli-engine now aborts a signal instead of exiting, but done_prepare only threads that parent signal into routine verifier.validate and the DONE-required runCloseoutPhase. The later doneClosure/reviewAssurance/runtimeChange/cleanTree/produceCommand runCloseoutPhase calls do not receive rawArgs.abortSignal, so an explicit max expiry during those phases is logged but does not terminate or structure the result. Even inside DONE-required validation, a parent CliWatchdogTimeoutError is not a DonePreparePhaseTimeoutError, so the catch falls through to `result=blocked` without timeoutLayer instead of `result=timed_out` with idle|max. The watchdog also has no top-level Promise.race fallback, so any uncooperative/synchronous done_prepare segment can outlive the absolute max. Thread/race the CLI watchdog across the whole handler and classify its reason before the generic blocked path; verify nonzero JSON outcomes for idle and max in both routine and post-validation closeout phases.
findings.resolvedReason: Source correction: the reviewer subclaim that later doneClosure/reviewAssurance/runtimeChange/cleanTree/produceCommand calls lacked the parent signal was disproven; every current call already passed rawArgs.abortSignal before this fix, so no false repro or worker redesign was used. Verified gaps: a parent CliWatchdogTimeoutError inside DONE-required closeout fell through generic blocked classification; closeout segments lacked explicit parent deadline checkpoints; and Promise.race could return before cooperative child/lock cleanup settled. Fix: all closeout segments now receive the full parent timeout control, check signal/deadline before and after work, classify parent idle|max as executed/timed_out at the active phase, abort cooperatively and await task/child settlement, while bounded sync-child wrappers enforce the first safe boundary. findings.desc: The additive done_prepare JSON defaults misclassify any transcript that blocks before validation. `donePrepareJsonResult` now fills missing fields with disposition=skipped_explicitly, result=blocked/not_run, existingEvidenceBasis=missing, but `skipped_explicitly` is contractually reserved for validate=false. A merge/preflight/stale-evidence blocker did not explicitly skip validation and its existing evidence basis was never evaluated, so the emitted structure asserts false facts. Preserve nullable/not_applicable fields for pre-validation blockers, or evaluate and emit a distinct disposition that does not claim an explicit operator skip.
findings.resolvedReason: Repro: request done_prepare --json for a nonexistent/unreadable story so preflight blocks before validation; prior additive defaults incorrectly emitted disposition=skipped_explicitly and existingEvidenceBasis=missing despite neither fact being observed. Root cause: donePrepareJsonResult synthesized validation fields whenever transcript tokens were absent. Fix: disposition, result, existingEvidenceBasis, timeoutLayer, and refusalReasons are emitted only when explicitly present in the transcript; explicit timeoutLayer=null remains distinguishable. validate=false, reuse, and execution paths retain their exact observed fields. The CHK-002 evidence map is shifted: happy:1 points to reuse-disabled execution (the edge:0 requirement), edge:0 points to validate=false (edge:1), edge:1 to canonical mutations (adversarial:0), edge:2 to lineage, edge:3 to malformed evidence, and adversarial:2 to generic output fields. More importantly, done-prepare-closure-heartbeat-smoke.ts:326-345 does not exercise actual exact-HEAD versus trusted-descendant reuse separately; reuse disabled only asserts a progress line, not disposition=executed or evidence refresh. done-required-validation-smoke.ts:429-655 lacks independent evidence-schema mutation, proof-admissibility failure mutation, non-ancestor HEAD, and metadata-like-outside-allowlist cases required by CHK-002 adversarial:0/2. The timeout matrices at validate-progress-heartbeat-smoke.ts:277-399 use wide timing margins rather than just-before/just-after command/phase/idle/max races; descendant ESRCH is asserted only for command timeout, while CHK-003 adversarial:0 requires descendant-tree termination separately for command, phase, idle, and max. No test emits heartbeat concurrently with abort/exit/error or asserts no post-terminal heartbeat/duplicate evidence. Add the missing matrix rows/race instrumentation, assert disabled-reuse terminal fields and refreshed receipt, and remap each verificationEvidence intentRef to its actual assertion before accepting coverage.

findings.desc: Post-validation closeout watchdog blocks overwrite already-observed validation facts. `cliWatchdogTimeoutBlock` always emits `disposition=executed` and `existingEvidenceBasis=stale`, even when done_prepare ran with validate=false and had already recorded `disposition=skipped_explicitly` plus a computed missing/fresh/stale basis. The new post-validation timeout smoke uses exactly validate=false/dryRun but asserts the fabricated executed disposition, locking in the contradiction. Keep overall `result=timed_out`/timeoutLayer=idle|max, but carry the validation disposition and evidence basis observed at the validate step (or separate validation outcome from overall command outcome). This is distinct from the fixed preflight case: here the fields were observed and are then replaced with false values.
findings.resolvedReason: Repro: run validate=false to observe disposition=skipped_explicitly/result=not_run with the actual existingEvidenceBasis/refusalReasons, then force a later doneClosure idle or max timeout. The prior timeout block overwrote that context with fabricated disposition=executed and basis=stale. Root cause: cliWatchdogTimeoutBlock constructed a fresh generic validation terminal instead of carrying the already-observed validate step context. Fix: parse the completed validate step into an ObservedValidationTerminalContext; later closeout watchdog blocks preserve disposition, evidence basis, and refusals, append the real CLI timeout refusal, and change only result/timeoutLayer to timed_out/idle|max. ReproTest: node packages/main/dist/tasks/done-prepare-closure-heartbeat-smoke.js. PASS at REVIEW HEAD 7ffa19b; baseline-vs-timeout assertions cover idle and max, singular JSON, nonzero status, no story-evidence mutation, and immediate rerun.

findings.desc: Round-3 cleanup/race/lineage matrices pass, but the core top-level budget regression still lacks an assertion that can detect omitted closeout phases. In done-prepare-closure-heartbeat-smoke.ts:90-100 the fixture selects DONE-required phase=1,500,000ms and global phase=1,400,000ms, yet only asserts total >= 1,500,000 + 330,000. An implementation summing routine validation plus DONE-required while omitting all five other enabled closeout phases would still pass, contrary to CHK-001:edge:4. CHK-001:edge:3 also claims both DONE entry paths use derived command-specific maxima, but tests only assert story_get stays 900,000ms; there is no exact commandCliMaxBudget assertion for done_required_validate or done_prepare. Add exact expected totals for validate=true required-policy, validate=false, no-policy, global override, and phase-specific override combinations, plus exact derived maxima for both DONE entry paths. Also correct CHK-002:happy:0 evidence wording or add an actual exact-HEAD done_prepare fixture: seedDoneRequiredViaCli auto-commits evidence, so the current integration run proves trusted-metadata-descendant reuse, while exact-head is only covered at the evaluator unit level.

Root cause: evidence described broad budget coverage without exact arithmetic for every enabled phase and the CHK-002 reuse notes conflated evaluator exact-HEAD with CLI metadata auto-commit lineage. Fix: exact totals now use six unique phase overrides plus a global override and assert routine sequential budget plus each enabled phase exactly once: five common closeout phases always, DONE-required only when required+validate, routine only when validate. Evidence correction: CHK-002 happy:0 now points to the evaluator exact-HEAD assertion; happy:1 points to actual done_prepare CLI integration, whose evidence auto-commit correctly proves trusted-story-metadata-descendant rather than exact HEAD. findings.desc: Routine done_prepare can still misclassify an explicit CLI max deadline as an ordinary validation failure. cli-engine passes both deadlineAt and an AbortSignal, but the validation runner independently shortens its command timer to deadlineAt (validation-executor.ts:309-314). If that timer settles before the polling watchdog aborts the signal—which is deterministic for MAX values not aligned with the watchdog interval, e.g. 1005ms with a 251ms poll—the verifier returns a failed/timed-out routine result while abortSignal.reason is still empty. done-prepare.ts:1651 only derives routineTimeoutLayer from the signal, then lines 1657-1663 take the generic parsed failure path, omitting disposition=executed, result=timed_out, timeoutLayer=max and existingEvidenceBasis. The new max smoke uses 180ms with a 45ms interval, aligning poll and deadline and masking this window. Treat Date.now() >= rawArgs.deadlineAt as max using rawArgs.deadlineError even before the signal fires, or propagate a named max-deadline reason through executeValidationPlan; add a deliberately non-divisible max fixture proving JSON classification and exit/event behavior.
findings.resolvedReason: Repro: configure a silent routine validate command longer than LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS=1005 while the CLI watchdog polls every floor(1005/4)=251ms. The command deadline could settle between watchdog ticks before abortSignal carried a named reason, so routine validation returned generic failure instead of timed_out/max. Root cause: cli-engine created deadlineError but done_prepare/verifier/ExecuteValidationPlan propagated only deadlineAt; the runner therefore lost the controlling deadline source. Fix: deadlineError now flows cli-engine -> done_prepare -> verifier -> ExecuteValidationPlan -> command options; after child cleanup, a deadline-owned timedOut result throws the named max error for structured classification. ReproTest: node packages/main/dist/tasks/validate-progress-heartbeat-smoke.js. PASS at REVIEW HEAD 7ffa19b; the 1005/251 real CLI regression asserts status=blocked, result=timed_out, timeoutLayer=max, existingEvidenceBasis=stale, exit 1, no generic validation-failed reason, and immediate successful rerun cleanup.

findings.desc: A remaining no-invented-fields gap exists for `validate=true,dryRun=true`. That branch records only `planned mutation skipped: dryRun does not run lattice validate`, so `observedValidationTerminalContext` correctly returns undefined. If a later closeout phase hits idle/max, `cliWatchdogTimeoutBlock` nevertheless falls back to disposition=executed and existingEvidenceBasis=stale, even though validation did not execute and the evidence basis was never evaluated. This is the same false-fact class F-006 prohibited, now reachable after the validate step. When validationContext is absent, emit only the observed overall timeout fields (result/refusalReasons/timeoutLayer) and omit disposition/basis, or explicitly record a truthful dry-run validation context before closeout.
findings.resolvedReason: Repro: run done_prepare --validate=true --dryRun=true --json, force a later doneClosure idle timeout, and inspect the terminal JSON. Because dryRun skips actual validation, there is no observed validation terminal context; the old path nevertheless emitted disposition=executed, existingEvidenceBasis=stale, and a synthetic refusalReasons entry. Root cause: cliWatchdogTimeoutBlock used fallback executed/stale values and always constructed refusalReasons when validationContext was undefined. Fix: the watchdog now conditionally composes terminal context—when observed validationContext exists it preserves disposition/evidence basis/refusals and appends the real watchdog refusal; when none exists it emits only the true result=timed_out and timeoutLayer=idle|max plus the ordinary blocked reason. ReproTest: npm --prefix packages/main run build; node packages/main/dist/tasks/done-prepare-closure-heartbeat-smoke.js; node scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs. PASS at REVIEW HEAD 2155e94; validate=true+dryRun JSON exits nonzero, reports blockedAt=doneClosure/result=timed_out/timeoutLayer=idle, emits one parseable object, and asserts disposition/existingEvidenceBasis/refusalReasons are absent, while existing validate=false idle|max cases retain observed context. Additional independent focused verification found no separate finding ID but exposed a sync-child cleanup gap: phase-bounded execFileSync/execSync used default SIGTERM and a resistant child reproduced 5041ms. Commit 47eb092 switches only phase-controlled deadlines to SIGKILL; the closure smoke now uses a SIGTERM-resistant child, verifies phase-bounded return plus immediate reap/restore, and passed three consecutive runs.

findings.desc: The real CLI timeout matrix is flaky under the full focused sequence: running build -> done-prepare-closure-heartbeat -> validate-progress-heartbeat failed with `max !== command` at the command-timeout row, while immediately rerunning validate-progress-heartbeat alone passed. The row at validate-progress-heartbeat-smoke.ts:280 gives the command only 180ms but caps the entire CLI at 5000ms; under load, post-command evidence/git/CLI settlement can cross that outer cap, allowing the max watchdog to overwrite the intended command classification before output. This makes a required regression nondeterministic and can block REVIEW/TEST despite correct runtime behavior. Give command/phase attribution rows a much wider outer max and matching harness ceiling (well above worst observed process startup/evidence commit time), reserving tight max only for the explicit max row; optionally assert elapsed diagnostics on failure. Re-run the exact combined sequence repeatedly to demonstrate stability.
findings.resolvedReason: Repro: run build followed by the full focused sequence under host load; direct command/phase/idle rows used 3-5s outer LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS and 5-8s harness ceilings measured from CLI spawn, while the intended inner timeout began only after process startup and fixture work. The outer max could therefore win first and misclassify a command/phase/idle row as max. Root cause: the test harness conflated infrastructure startup budget with the timeout layer under test. Fix in d374c96740: define NON_MAX_OUTER_TIMEOUT_MS=120000 and NON_MAX_HARNESS_CEILING_MS=60000; apply them to direct pass/command/idle, command-descendant, done_prepare idle, outer-idle descendant, story heartbeat, true command-timeout, and all non-max immediate retries. Only rows explicitly testing max retain tight values: direct/done_prepare max=180ms, descendant max=700ms, named non-divisible max=1005ms. findings.desc: BUG-015 regression coverage is incomplete. The added budget block proves only direct done_required_validate (lines 382-390), not direct done_prepare. The timeout block (lines 414-450) proves stale-lock cleanup and capture-only behavior, but never creates a separate still-live validation lock to prove it is preserved, never immediately reruns capture after cleanup, and never combines the timeout with --write then reads evidence/live-smoke-transcript.json to prove the persisted timeout has exitCode:null/non-pass semantics. These are four explicit safety regressions requested for this round; without them a future change could delete an active validator lock, leave the command unusable after timeout, or serialize a timed-out capture as successful while the smoke remains green. findings.desc: BUG-015 remains reproducible for a supported explicit max override: liveSmokeCaptureBudget recognizes a direct `lattice done_required_validate`/`done_prepare` command but derives only the default/config phase budget and ignores the command's authoritative inherited `LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS`. The nested CLI honors that env at cli-engine.ts:1005-1014, while the capture timer arms the shorter value at done-required-timeout-budget.ts:127-144 and live-smoke-transcript.ts:516-518, so capture can SIGTERM/SIGKILL a still-legally-running closeout. Repro after build: `LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS=2147483647 node --input-type=module -e "import { liveSmokeCaptureBudget } from './packages/main/dist/core/done-required-timeout-budget.js'; const b=liveSmokeCaptureBudget(process.cwd(),'lattice done_required_validate --storyId=B-c163',process.env); console.log(JSON.stringify({explicitMax:Number(process.env.LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS),capture:b})); if (!(b.timeoutMs < Number(process.env.LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS))) process.exit(2);"` prints explicitMax=2147483647 versus capture.timeoutMs=1520000. This contradicts the decisions contract that explicit LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS remains authoritative and the Round-8 requirement that capture never impose a shorter ceiling on a recognized closeout command. Include the clamped explicit max in the recognized-command legal ceiling (and account deliberately for allowed inline env assignments), while preserving the 60s arbitrary-command ceiling and lower-only LATTICE_LIVE_SMOKE_CAPTURE_TIMEOUT_MS override. The persisted candidate digest 79fc8a964ff94df0740750b1b0a967b329c8274d211a1909c76141ebd26e13ea is stale; exact current local recomputation after review_run_start is 286e849c16a844a368a84188612e86ae40e370453b60d8f00f1a3109c7fff402; corpus digest is unchanged.

BUG-015 still allows an arbitrary executable to obtain the derived closeout timeout through an accepted shell environment prefix. recognizedLiveSmokeCommand accepts unrestricted NAME=value assignments before lattice. Because runCapture later executes through shell:true, PATH=/tmp/fake:$PATH lattice done_required_validate resolves /tmp/fake/lattice, and LD_PRELOAD=/tmp/arbitrary.so lattice done_required_validate injects arbitrary code, yet both are classified as recognized closeout commands. Repro after build: importing liveSmokeCaptureBudget for node arbitrary.js returns 60000, while PATH=/tmp/fake:$PATH lattice done_required_validate --storyId=B-c163 and LD_PRELOAD=/tmp/arbitrary.so lattice done_required_validate --storyId=B-c163 each return recognizedCommand=done_required_validate and timeoutMs=1520000 in this repo. This violates the fixed 60-second arbitrary-command safety ceiling and the direct-command recognition boundary. Reject inline environment assignments for the widened path, or narrowly allowlist inert assignments such as LATTICE_SESSION_ID while rejecting executable-resolution/runtime-injection variables and resolving the intended lattice executable before granting the derived budget. Add PATH and LD_PRELOAD/NODE_OPTIONS adversarial budget assertions. The persisted candidate digest 79fc8a964ff94df0740750b1b0a967b329c8274d211a1909c76141ebd26e13ea is stale; the last independently recomputed digest before the concurrent finding commits was 286e849c16a844a368a84188612e86ae40e370453b60d8f00f1a3109c7fff402, so owner must reroute for the exact current digest; corpus digest is unchanged.

findings.desc: The inherited-max fix still lets the outer live-smoke wrapper terminate before the nested closeout reaches its authoritative deadline and cleanup. `liveSmokeCaptureBudget` sets the handler timer to exactly inherited `LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS` (done-required-timeout-budget.ts:200-215), while the nested done_required_validate/done_prepare starts its own same-duration watchdog only after process spawn and CLI startup. More directly, cli-engine.ts:1005-1013 applies the same explicit max to the outer `live_smoke_transcript` invocation, overriding commandCliMaxBudget's intended capture+30s grace. Repro after build: `LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS=1000 node --input-type=module -e "import { resolve } from 'node:path'; import { liveSmokeCaptureBudget, commandCliMaxBudget, NODE_TIMER_MAX_MS } from './packages/main/dist/core/done-required-timeout-budget.js'; const cmd=resolve('bin/lattice.js')+' done_required_validate --storyId=B-c163 --json'; const capture=liveSmokeCaptureBudget(process.cwd(),cmd,process.env); const derivedOuter=commandCliMaxBudget(process.cwd(),'live_smoke_transcript',{capture:cmd}); const explicit=Math.min(NODE_TIMER_MAX_MS,Math.floor(Number(process.env.LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS))); console.log(JSON.stringify({captureTimeoutMs:capture.timeoutMs,derivedOuterTimeoutMs:derivedOuter.timeoutMs,effectiveOuterCliTimeoutMs:explicit,effectiveNestedCliTimeoutMs:explicit})); if (!(capture.timeoutMs===explicit && explicit<derivedOuter.timeoutMs)) process.exit(2);"` prints capture=1000, derivedOuter=31000, but effective outer CLI=1000 and effective nested CLI=1000. Since the outer watchdog starts before spawn and the handler timer starts before nested CLI initialization, equality is an effective shorter ceiling; structured nested timeout output/cleanup can be preempted. Preserve the nested inherited max as authoritative, but give the handler a bounded post-deadline cleanup/reap grace and make the outer live_smoke CLI use its derived wrapper budget (which already incorporates inherited max) rather than reapplying the raw explicit max. `LATTICE_LIVE_SMOKE_CAPTURE_TIMEOUT_MS` may intentionally remain lower-only. Inline executable-affecting env assignments correctly remain unrecognized/60s and must stay so.

The injection boundary is fixed, but the widened budget rejects the repository actual standard global lattice executable, so a normal direct `lattice done_required_validate` capture still receives only 60000ms. In trustedLatticeExecutable, activeEntrypoint is accepted as global only when its realpath matches /node_modules/@lattice/core/dist/cli.js. Here `command -v lattice` is /Users/jek/.nvm/versions/node/v22.13.0/bin/lattice and its realpath is /Users/jek/Documents/Work/proofbound/packages/main/dist/cli.js, which is the active verified global CLI but does not match that regex and is outside the story worktree root. Repro after build: set process.argv[1] to that actual shim and call liveSmokeCaptureBudget(process.cwd(), `lattice done_required_validate --storyId=B-c163`, process.env); result is timeoutMs=60000, source=fixed-arbitrary-command, recognizedCommand=null. The project candidate does not rescue normal use: worktree bin/lattice.js is tracked mode 100644, while the smoke creates a synthetic chmod 0755 bin/lattice.js, so its positive case does not represent either shipped entrypoint. This leaves the original long direct closeout capture path functionally unrecognized despite the new safety parser. Resolve the global/project executable through the existing runtime entrypoint/realpath contract, or safely accept the current running CLI realpath when the PATH executable resolves to that same verified entrypoint; add a regression using the actual global-symlink layout rather than only a chmod fixture. PATH/LD_PRELOAD/NODE_OPTIONS/inline timeout assignments and ;, &&, pipe, redirect, command substitution, backtick and newline composition all independently remained at 60000ms in this review.

Each project candidate is resolved and then compared against a candidate list containing its own realpath, so chmod or symlink makes it self-authorizing even when it does not equal the active CLI. Deterministic repro after build in a fresh temp root with activeCliEntrypoint set to the real global CLI: (1) create root/bin/lattice.js containing an arbitrary shell script and chmod 0755; liveSmokeCaptureBudget(root, `<that path> done_required_validate --storyId=B-test`, env, active) returns recognizedCommand=done_required_validate, source=derived-done-required-command, timeoutMs=30000 instead of fixed 60000; (2) symlink root/bin/lattice.js to process.execPath and the same call again recognizes Node itself and grants the derived budget. The realpaths differ from active `/Users/jek/Documents/Work/proofbound/packages/main/dist/cli.js`. Remove the independent project-path candidates and require resolvedExecutable === resolved activeCliEntrypoint; a project CLI is naturally accepted when it is the active entrypoint. Add explicit chmod-fake and project-bin-symlink-to-node negatives. Positive actual `command -v lattice` resolves and receives 1520000ms; PATH/LD_PRELOAD/NODE_OPTIONS/inline timeout assignments plus semicolon, &&, pipe, redirect, command substitution, backticks and newline remain 60000ms. Build, live-smoke smoke, command-catalog smoke and process-fact fingerprint contract pass.

findings.desc: Layer ordering is correct for ordinary inherited maxima, but collapses at the supported Node timer clamp: `positiveInt` clamps the nested inherited max to NODE_TIMER_MAX_MS, then both `safeTimeoutSum([nested, cleanupGrace])` and the outer wrapper sum saturate to the same NODE_TIMER_MAX_MS. Repro after build: `ACTIVE=$(realpath "$(command -v lattice)") node --input-type=module -e "import { liveSmokeCaptureBudget,effectiveCommandCliMaxBudget,NODE_TIMER_MAX_MS } from './packages/main/dist/core/done-required-timeout-budget.js'; const active=process.env.ACTIVE,cmd='lattice done_required_validate --storyId=B-c163 --json',env={...process.env,LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS:String(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER)}; const c=liveSmokeCaptureBudget(process.cwd(),cmd,env,active); const o=effectiveCommandCliMaxBudget(process.cwd(),'live_smoke_transcript',{capture:cmd},env,active); console.log(JSON.stringify({nested:c.nestedMaxTimeoutMs,capture:c.timeoutMs,outer:o.timeoutMs,nodeMax:NODE_TIMER_MAX_MS}));"` prints nested=capture=outer=2147483647. Because the outer CLI watchdog starts before capture spawn and the capture timer starts before nested CLI initialization, equal numeric ceilings still allow the outer layer to fire first and preempt the intended nested structured timeout plus TERM/KILL/reap cleanup. This affects only the ~24.8-day saturation edge and remains fail-closed, so severity is medium, but it does not satisfy the requested ordered/fail-closed clamp boundary. Reserve wrapper grace below the clamp (including ensuring the nested child receives the reserved effective max), or implement an explicit saturated-edge policy/test that guarantees cleanup and structured outcome without relying on equal-start timers. Ordinary 1000ms evidence is correct: nested=1000, capture=4000, outer=34000, unrelated command=1000; focused live-smoke/process-fact/retired-vocabulary tests all pass.

Round 11 still lacks a mechanical regression proving the handler passes the saturation-adjusted nested max into the spawned child. The new assertions at live-smoke-transcript-smoke.ts:471-489 call liveSmokeCaptureBudget/effectiveCommandCliMaxBudget directly and validate requestedNestedMaxTimeoutMs, nestedMaxTimeoutMs, capture, and outer values, but no handler invocation runs a recognized trusted lattice command under MAX_SAFE and observes the child environment. The handler wiring at live-smoke-transcript.ts:519-522 could be removed, use requestedNestedMaxTimeoutMs instead of nestedMaxTimeoutMs, or omit the env override entirely while every added smoke assertion remains green. Existing handler timeout/write/retry tests use an arbitrary Node command and only LATTICE_LIVE_SMOKE_CAPTURE_TIMEOUT_MS, so they do not cover this path. Build, compiled live-smoke smoke, and process-fact contract all pass, confirming this is a verified coverage gap rather than a current runtime failure.

findings.desc: The layered-grace fix is applied only when inherited `LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS` is present; trusted closeout captures using the normal derived/configured budget still arm the handler at exactly the nested CLI max, so the handler timer starts earlier and can preempt nested structured timeout/cleanup. Default repro after build: `env -u LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS ACTIVE=$(realpath "$(command -v lattice)") node --input-type=module -e "import { liveSmokeCaptureBudget,effectiveCommandCliMaxBudget,commandCliMaxBudget } from './packages/main/dist/core/done-required-timeout-budget.js'; process.argv[1]=process.env.ACTIVE; const cmd='lattice done_required_validate --storyId=B-c163 --json'; const nested=commandCliMaxBudget(process.cwd(),'done_required_validate',{},process.env).timeoutMs; const capture=liveSmokeCaptureBudget(process.cwd(),cmd,process.env); const outer=effectiveCommandCliMaxBudget(process.cwd(),'live_smoke_transcript',{capture:cmd},process.env).timeoutMs; console.log(JSON.stringify({nested,capture:capture.timeoutMs,outer,strict:nested<capture.timeoutMs&&capture.timeoutMs<outer,source:capture.source}));"` prints nested=1520000, capture=1520000, outer=1550000, strict=false. The same omission reappears at a configured/phase-derived Node saturation without LATTICE_MAX: setting `LATTICE_DONE_PREPARE_DONE_CLOSURE_TIMEOUT_MS=Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` yields nested=capture=outer=2147483647 and saturationAdjusted=false. ce35dc7f7c correctly adjusts/passes the child env for inherited-max saturation, reports requested/effective/saturation fields, preserves unrelated raw explicit max, and blocks project-path self-authorization, but it does not generalize nested effective-max reservation to ordinary derived/configured budgets. Compute a requested/effective nested business bound for every recognized closeout capture, add cleanup grace regardless of source, reserve both grace layers at saturation, and pass an adjusted child `LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS` whenever the effective nested bound differs from what the nested CLI would otherwise derive. Add default-derived and phase/config-saturated strict-order assertions plus an actual child-env observation.

Distinct from F-021/F-022: the async live-smoke capture can let the CLI terminate successfully before its timeout Promise settles. runCapture unrefs timeoutTimer, heartbeatTimer, and the 250ms forceKill timer. When the 100ms timeout sends SIGTERM and the direct child closes promptly, child close records closed=true but intentionally does not call finish because timedOut=true; the only remaining path to finish is the unref force-kill timer. The local CLI entry calls runCli().catch(...) without top-level await, so no referenced handle keeps the process alive. Deterministic real CLI repro after build, three consecutive runs: `LATTICE_LIVE_SMOKE_CAPTURE_TIMEOUT_MS=100 node packages/main/dist/cli.js live_smoke_transcript {"storyId":"B-c163","capture":"sleep 5","json":true}` prints only `[0.1s] running live_smoke_transcript...`, exits 0, emits zero stdout bytes, never prints done, and records no structured timeout JSON. The compiled focused smoke also failed once in this review with Node `Warning: Detected unsettled top-level await` at its separate-live-lock handler await, then passed on retries, confirming the same load-sensitive liveness race. Keep a referenced cleanup deadline until finish, or settle directly on close after timedOut while ensuring the process group has been terminated/reaped and all timers/listeners are cleared; add an actual CLI regression asserting non-silent structured timeout completion and non-success exit semantics. F-016/F-018/F-019 trust conditions themselves now pass: exact global realpath widens, chmod fake and PATH symlink-to-Node remain 60s, the active-entrypoint function parameter seam is removed, and all inline env/composition negatives remain 60s. Build, command-catalog, process-fact/fingerprint contract pass; live-smoke smoke is flaky as described.
